question: What triggers urine leakage in a patient with stress incontinence?
explanation: Physical activities that increase intra-abdominal pressure force urine out when pelvic support is weak. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h1)

question: How does stress incontinence differ from urge incontinence?

options.A: It only affects male patients rather than female patients
options.B: It occurs exclusively during sleep instead of waking hours
options.C: It is caused by physical pressure rather than sudden bladder muscle contractions
options.D: It involves complete inability to produce urine rather than leakage

explanation: Stress incontinence is a mechanical problem of support, while urge incontinence involves involuntary bladder muscle contractions. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h1)

question: Which muscle group forms the primary supportive sling for the pelvic organs?
explanation: The levator ani group provides the main structural floor supporting the bladder and urethra. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the urethral sphincters in urinary continence?

options.A: To remain contracted and keep the urinary channel closed at rest
options.B: To generate the force needed to empty the bladder completely
options.C: To transmit nerve signals from the spinal cord to the brain
options.D: To produce hormones that regulate daily urine production volume

explanation: Sphincters act as tight valves that maintain closure until purposeful urination occurs. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h2)

question: What is urethral hypermobility in the context of stress incontinence?

options.A: Complete rigidity of the urinary sphincter muscle fibers
options.B: Excessive downward movement of the bladder neck during pressure
options.C: Involuntary spasms of the bladder wall muscle
options.D: Rapid bacterial infection traveling up the urinary tract

explanation: Hypermobility means the support structures have slackened, allowing the urethra to drop abnormally during strain. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h3)

question: Why does weakening of the pelvic floor lead directly to urine leakage?

options.A: It blocks the normal flow of blood to the bladder walls
options.B: It causes the bladder to shrink to a much smaller size
options.C: It prevents proper pressure transmission to close the urethra
options.D: It stops the kidneys from filtering waste products properly

explanation: Without a firm backstop from supportive tissues, increased abdominal pressure pushes urine out past the unsupported urethra. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h3)

question: Which factor is a primary cause of pelvic floor trauma leading to stress incontinence?
explanation: The stretching and physical strain of vaginal delivery frequently damages pelvic support tissues and nerves. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h4)

question: How does chronic coughing contribute to the development of stress incontinence?

options.A: By placing repetitive downward strain on the pelvic floor muscles
options.B: By increasing overall daily urine production in the kidneys
options.C: By irritating the inner lining of the urinary bladder
options.D: By weakening the nerve connections in the lower spinal cord

explanation: Repeated forceful coughs repeatedly stress and fatigue the pelvic support structures until they weaken. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h4)

question: What is the purpose of a bladder diary during clinical assessment?

options.A: To measure exact muscle strength in the pelvic floor
options.B: To record daily fluid intake and episodes of leakage
options.C: To check blood pressure changes during urination
options.D: To test for bacterial infections in the urine sample

explanation: A bladder diary tracks patterns of fluid consumption and incontinence events over multiple days. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h5)

question: How is a basic cough stress test performed during a physical exam?

options.A: The nurse listens to the abdomen with a stethoscope while coughing
options.B: The patient coughs with a full bladder while observing for leakage
options.C: The patient drinks large volumes of water until coughing starts
options.D: The patient holds their breath while running on a treadmill

explanation: Observing immediate urine loss during a cough confirms the mechanical nature of stress incontinence. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of teaching Kegel exercises to a patient?

options.A: To reduce nighttime urine production by the kidneys
options.B: To relax the abdominal wall during deep breathing exercises
options.C: To strengthen the pelvic floor muscles supporting the urethra
options.D: To expand the total physical capacity of the bladder muscle

explanation: Kegels build strength in the levator ani muscles to improve structural support around the urethra. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h6)

question: Which instruction is most important when teaching a patient how to perform Kegel exercises?

options.A: Hold your breath tightly for one full minute during each contraction
options.B: Perform the exercises only while standing up in front of a mirror
options.C: Drink two glasses of water immediately before starting your routine
options.D: Avoid contracting your abdominal, thigh, or buttock muscles at the same time

explanation: Isolating the pelvic floor ensures the correct muscle group is being strengthened without substituting other muscle groups. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h6)

question: What is the most common surgical procedure performed for stress urinary incontinence?
explanation: Mid-urethral slings provide a supportive hammock under the urethra to prevent downward displacement during pressure. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h7)

question: Why might a doctor prescribe topical estrogen to a postmenopausal patient with stress incontinence?

options.A: To stimulate rapid weight loss and reduce abdominal pressure
options.B: To improve the health and elasticity of the urethral tissues
options.C: To increase the total volume of urine held in the kidneys
options.D: To cause temporary paralysis of the bladder wall muscles

explanation: Estrogen helps maintain mucosal thickness and vascularity in the urogenital tissues, supporting closure. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common complication associated with chronic untreated stress incontinence?
explanation: Stress incontinence affects lower urinary tract support, not kidney filtration function, so kidney failure is not a typical complication. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h8)

question: What is a key nursing priority when educating a patient recovering from a mid-urethral sling procedure?

options.A: Telling them pelvic floor exercises are no longer necessary
options.B: Instructing them to stop drinking all fluids for three months
options.C: Encouraging heavy lifting immediately to test the new sling
options.D: Teaching them to watch for signs of urinary retention or infection

explanation: Postoperative monitoring for normal voiding and infection prevention is essential after urinary tract surgery. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h8)
